# 因明入正理論疏

**ID:** T1840
**Volume:** T44
**Category:** 論集部類
**Original Category:** 論疏部
**Byline:** 唐 窺基撰
**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 632–682
**Juans:** 3
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T1840

## Contributors
- 窺基 (A001019)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The single most important and influential commentary on Buddhist logic in the East Asian tradition: a comprehensive sub-commentary in three *juǎn* on Śaṅkarasvāmin's *Nyāyapraveśa* [KR6o0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0003), composed by [窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) (Kuījī, 632–682), the principal disciple of [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) (Xuánzàng) and the founder of the Cí'ēn 慈恩 (also called Fǎxiàng 法相) school of East Asian Yogācāra. Universally referred to in the tradition as the "Great Commentary" (大疏 *Dà-shū*) — to distinguish it from Wénguǐ's earlier *shū* [KR6o0021](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0021) — Kuījī's commentary became the orthodox reference work for *yīnmíng* in China, Korea, and Japan: every subsequent commentator on the *Rù lùn* takes the *Dà-shū* as their primary point of reference, whether to gloss it (as in the entire Cí'ēn lineage of Huìzhǎo [KR6o0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0018), [KR6o0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0019), [KR6o0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0022) and Zhìzhōu [KR6o0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0023), [KR6o0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0024), [KR6o0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0025)), to challenge it, or, in Japan, to produce yet larger sub-commentaries on it (Zenju 善珠's *Myōtō shō* [KR6o0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0009) and Zōshun 藏俊's *Daisho shō* [KR6o0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0010) and others).

**Abstract**

The opening preface narrates a brief intellectual history of Indian thought down to the rise of Buddhist logic, identifying [商羯羅主菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%95%86%E7%BE%AF%E7%BE%85%E4%B8%BB%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) (Śaṅkarasvāmin, here: 商羯羅) as the disciple of 域龍 (Dignāga) and the author of the *Rù lùn*; it then connects the work's transmission to Kuījī's "親教三藏大師" (his own personal teacher, the Tripiṭaka master Xuánzàng) and his journey to India. The body of the *Dà-shū* glosses the *Rù lùn* line by line, expanding extensively on each of the four canonical operations (能立, 似能立, 能破, 似能破) and the two cognitive operations (現量, 比量), introducing copious distinctions in the discussion of fallacies, especially the famous treatment of *xiāngwéi* 相違 (contradiction) of which the *Rù lùn* identifies four kinds (法自相相違, 法差別相違, 有法自相相違, 有法差別相違) — Kuījī's treatment of these came to be regarded as so authoritative that an entire later sub-genre of "four contradictions" (四相違) commentaries developed around it [KR6o0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0014), [KR6o0015](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0015), [KR6o0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0016), [KR6o0017](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0017). The text is incomplete: only the upper *juǎn* (卷上) and middle *juǎn* (卷中) survive in full, with the third (卷下) preserved only as a fragment ending mid-sentence. The Cí'ēn tradition treated this as the unfinished masterwork of Kuījī's *yīnmíng* studies, and devoted significant effort to "completing" it — particularly Huìzhǎo's *Yìduàn* [KR6o0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0018), *Yì-zuǎn-yào* [KR6o0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0019), and *Xù-shū* [KR6o0022](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0022) all act, in their different ways, as continuations or completions of the missing portions. Composition is normally placed in Kuījī's middle period at the Dà Cí'ēn-sì 大慈恩寺, sometime between 660 and his death in 682.
